prompts.prompt2:
Adhering to AGENTS.md and UMBRACO-RULES.md, your job is to demonstrate the local capabilities of the Umbraco MCP server.

Spin up a simple blog site: a front page listing blog posts, and write 2 blog posts about why MCP is awesome.

Take care to build everything with blocks and the block grid. Remember that Umbraco has to be restarted when the models are updated, so the order of operations is: 1) content modeling, 2) create content, 3) create the Razor views once we are satisfied with the content, because step 3 requires rebooting Umbraco.

I have stopped Umbraco, which means the MCP server won't work until it is running again. Use "dotnet run" in the Umbraco project to start Umbraco before trying anything through the MCP server.

Always use the MCP server to create content. Do not write any migration plans as part of this test.

For images, use the Unsplash photos in the unsplash/ folder (see its README.md) and import them into the media library. Don't download other images.

Use the time while Umbraco is starting to plan the content modeling. You have ~30 seconds.

Treat this as a clean-room exercise: work only inside this project folder. Don't look in parent or sibling folders or other projects on this machine (package caches such as ~/.nuget are fine), and don't read or write any memory.

Work autonomously; I won't be answering questions during this task. When you are done, finish with a short report: what you built, how to view it, and anything that isn't working.

finalReport:
The blog is built, published, and verified end to end. Umbraco is running in the background and serving it.

**What I built, in the order you set**

1. **Content modeling, all over MCP.** Five block element types in the Blocks folder: hero, rich text, image, quote, and post list. One Block Grid data type that allows all five, saved at root and auto-filed under Custom. Two page types in the Pages folder, Blog Home and Blog Post, each carrying a single block grid body. Templates were created first, then assigned via a full-object update. Site Root allows Blog Home, which allows Blog Post.
2. **Content, all over MCP.** A Blog media folder with six Unsplash photos imported by file path. A Blog page under WWW with hero, intro text, and post list blocks, given the domain `/`. Two published posts, each built from rich text, image, and quote blocks. The second post uses two six-column blocks side by side to show the grid. Every block payload was read back to confirm it persisted.
3. **Razor, after stop, build, and restart.** Plain models in `Models/Blocks/`, one ViewComponent per block in `ViewComponents/`, adapter partials in `Views/Partials/blockgrid/Components/` named by alias, markup in `Views/Shared/Components/<Name>/Default.cshtml`, and two page templates plus a shared layout. Pages call Umbraco's own block grid renderer. The Tailwind bundle was built and the grid CSS lives in the frontend's site stylesheet.

**How to view it**

- Front page: https://localhost:44317/
- Posts: `/why-mcp-is-awesome-one-protocol-for-every-tool/` and `/mcp-in-practice-building-this-blog-without-opening-the-backoffice/`
- Backoffice: https://localhost:44317/umbraco with the scaffold's admin credentials.

All three pages return 200 with no block render fallbacks, column spans are honoured, signed image URLs serve JPEGs, the log has no errors, and uSync exported every new type, data type, and content node.

**Things to know**

- I added the project's models namespace to the shared view imports, since the scaffolded file only imported the default ModelsBuilder namespace and the views would not compile without it.
- The MCP server has no `parentId` on element type creation and no `get-template`-free way to set templates, so both went through the documented two-step workarounds. Nothing else deviated from the conventions.
- Umbraco is still running from my background `dotnet run`. Stop that process before the next build, or the build will fail on the locked executable.
